reviews.title: IPhone ios 27 mein split screen ka option aata hai kya?
reviews.text:
iPhone mein native system-wide **split screen** (ek sath do alag apps chalana) ka option nahi aata hai. Waise, abhi 2026 mein latest version iOS 20 chal raha hai, isliye iOS 27 aane mein abhi kaafi saal baaki hain.
Halanki, Apple iPhone par multitasking ke liye kuch dusre vikalp zaroor deta hai:
 * **Picture-in-Picture (PiP):** Video calls (FaceTime/WhatsApp) karne ya YouTube/Netflix par video dekhte waqt aap video ki screen ko chota karke background mein dusre apps chala sakte hain.
 * **Third-Party Browser Apps:** App Store par kuch aisi apps maujood hain (jaise Split Screen browser) jo ek hi screen par do alag-alag websites open karne ki suvidha deti hain, par ye feature aapke phone ki dusri apps (jaise WhatsApp aur Instagram ek sath) par kaam nahi karta.
Agar aapko proper split-screen ka experience chahiye, toh Apple abhi ye feature sirf apne iPads (iPadOS) mein 'Split View' ke naam se deta hai.
Nahi, abhi iOS 27 nahi aaya hai.
Abhi 2026 chal raha hai aur filhaal **iOS 20** latest version hai. Apple har saal September ke aas-paas ek naya mukhya iOS version launch karta hai. Agar yahi schedule chalta raha, toh iOS 27 aane mein abhi lagbhag 7 saal aur lagenge aur yeh **2033** ke aas-paas launch hoga.

reviews.title: Brilliant AI ruined by broken architecture. Leaving for Claude/ChatGPT
reviews.text:
I migrated my entire health and longevity project that helped me successful navigate a dire family health issue to Gemini after years with ChatGPT because Gemini’s medical and health data processing is genuinely superior. But Google’s latest "Notebook" integration on mobile is an absolute disaster, and I am being forced to leave the platform.

The workflow is completely broken. You cannot easily start a clean, isolated chat thread on mobile that benefits from your notebook’s sources while permanently saving new data back to it. Because I use a custom domain work account, Google completely firewalls the two tools. If I attach a notebook to a Gemini chat, it's a read-only dead end—the notebook retains absolutely zero memory of the conversation.

Forcing users into endless, chaotic chat threads or making them manually copy-paste data to keep a project updated defeats the entire purpose of AI. I have years of dense health history trapped in this ecosystem that I now have to manually extract using desktop workarounds just to migrate to Claude or back to ChatGPT. Google has the best underlying information engine, but they are completely losing the AI game because of atrocious, anti-user product design. Fix your workspace architecture.

reviews.title: An Interesting Alternative, but Not Always a Reliable One
reviews.text:
I have been using Google Gemini for some time now, and I do think it is an interesting alternative to competition. It often allows me to look at various topics from a different perspective, which is extremely valuable these days.

What I do not understand, however, is its occasional tendency to forget the rules or assumptions that were clearly established earlier. Unfortunately, hallucinations — even in the latest and supposedly “thinking” versions — still happen far too often. A fast answer is not necessarily a better answer. Sometimes no answer at all would be much better than a misleading one.

Google’s approach to the idea of actually getting what you pay for is a whole separate art form. There were months when I paid for the highest subscription tier — well over €100 — and Gemini still had no problem replying to my question with something along the lines of: “Try again later, resources are currently busy.”

I no longer pay for the highest-tier subscription, because I do not particularly enjoy being taken for a ride.

Even now, I still occasionally get messages saying that, this time, internet access has not been assigned and will not be assigned, even though it is essential to answer the question properly. The suggested solution? Start a new conversation.

The funny thing is that this usually works.

GPT does not play these kinds of games. At least not for now.

For learning and long reading sessions, a simple background (black, white, or clean minimal theme like ChatGPT) would be much better. The current visual style feels overdesigned rather than productivity-focused.

Also, the font style and letter spacing could be improved. A cleaner, softer font (cloud/simple type words) would reduce eye strain and improve readability.

Overall:
Gemini is powerful, but to be truly effective for study and focus, it needs a minimal, calm UI, simpler background options, and better font choices.

reviews.title: Marketing vs Reality: Why Gemini is a Regression in Dictation and Voice Tech
reviews.text: Google’s marketing of Gemini as an integrated AI experience is a fundamental misrepresentation of the software's actual state. The core issue is a complete failure in conversational mechanics; the voice mode is effectively unusable for natural speech because it lacks any sophisticated silence detection, leading to constant interruptions during necessary pauses for thought. This creates a high-friction interaction that is vastly inferior to competitors like ChatGPT. Furthermore, the supposed integration is a shallow shortcut system rather than a unified engine. There is an inexcusable performance gap between Gboard dictation, Gemini voice mode, and the standalone Recorder app. Users are forced into a fragmented workflow—recording in one app just to get stable transcription and then manually moving that data to Gemini—because the primary AI interface cannot handle basic continuous speech without speaking over the user. This technical decay extends to the Google Home ecosystem, which has become sluggish and unresponsive, where the Gemini rebranding serves only as a cosmetic mask for deep-seated latency. The arbitrary termination of support for functional hardware like the Nest Secure further proves that Google’s ecosystem has become a liability for the user. The current implementation of Gemini is a glitchy, fragmented disappointment that fails the most basic requirement of seamless, non-interruptive dictation.

reviews.text:
I was excited to try Gemini as a powerful AI assistant, but I’ve been deeply disappointed by how heavily censored and ideologically biased it is. Perfectly legitimate questions—especially around health, medicine, science, or anything even slightly controversial—are met with vague refusals, moral lecturing, or outright blocking of information with phrases like “I’m not able to help with that” or “this content may be harmful.”
Even when I ask for publicly available, peer-reviewed medical information or simply want a balanced summary of different viewpoints, Gemini often shuts the conversation down or gives an obviously one-sided answer that aligns with a narrow set of corporate-approved opinions. It feels less like an AI assistant and more like a nanny that’s afraid of offending someone.
For comparison, other models (Claude, Grok, Perplexity, etc.) are willing to engage with the same topics thoughtfully and transparently, citing sources and acknowledging uncertainty when it exists. Gemini’s extreme caution makes it practically unusable for serious research or even curious exploration.
Until Google dials back the censorship and trusts users to think for themselves, I can’t recommend Gemini. It’s a powerful engine trapped behind an overly paranoid filter. Very disappointing from a company that used to champion “organize the world’s information and make it universally accessible.”
